messages:
Maya: Quick sync — Q3 runtime plan needs a firm call: push kernel fusion + quantization, or prioritize KV prefetch + adaptive batching. Customer X flagged tail latency on chat as a blocker.
Jared: Can we do both in parallel? unclear on infra/dev headcount.
Lee: My vote is kv-prefetch first — biggest win on 95p for multi-turn chat right now. Kernel fusion is higher risk.
Noah: Bench data supports Lee: preliminary run shows ~18% 95p improvement on 8k sequences with prefetch enabled (internal link: https://perf.internal/bench/xf-8k).
Sam: Ops note: prefetch increases memory footprint and may impact Dedicated pool sizing. Need cost delta estimate before we commit.
Maya: OKR alignment: target is -20% 95p for chat 8k workloads. If we pick prefetch as the bet, launch criteria = 95p <= -20% AND cost delta <= 10% vs baseline.
Jared: Kernel fusion + 4-bit quant could hit cost goals faster but introduces model-quality risk and longer QA cycles.
Lee: Proposal: run dual canaries for 2 weeks: (A) kv-prefetch + adaptive batching, (B) kernel fusion + 4-bit quant + controlled fallback. Compare metrics and regressions.
Noah: Agree. Minimum metric set to capture:
``
- latency.p95 (ms)
- latency.p50 (ms)
- throughput.tokens_per_sec
- infra.cost_per_1M_tokens
- quality.semantic-score on eval set (2k prompts)
- error.rate (5xx / total)
```
Maya: Also add rollback criteria: quality drop >1.5% absolute OR error rate increase >0.5% => immediate rollback.
Sam: Who's owning canary monitoring? perf-bot can create groups but need a human owner for paging.
Noah: I'll own monitoring and dashboards. Will wire alerts for p95 regressions and error spikes.
Maya: Timeline: decision required by EOD Friday to slot into Q3 planning.
Jared: I'll scope dev tasks and post estimates by Thursday. Estimated dev effort: prefetch ~2.5w, fusion+quant ~4w, canary infra ~1w.
Lee: I'll open kernel-opt tickets and add perf test plans.
perf-bot: Canary created: group/canary-alpha id=a1b2c3 (owners: Noah).
Maya: Need CS aligned with Customer X SLA; @Noah please coordinate with CS to run customer prompts through canary.
Noah: Will coordinate. Also will run memory headroom tests — prefetch reported +6% GPU memory on 80B model in initial runs.
Sam: Ops question: does prefetch require sharded KV changes or new eviction logic?
Lee: Prefetch config to try (rough):
``
kv_prefetch:
  window_tokens: 1024
  parallel_reads: 4
  eviction_policy: lru
  max_prefetch_bytes: 512MB
```
Noah: We'll validate memory + throughput tradeoffs and post results to the canary dashboard.
Maya: Decision path: if prefetch meets launch criteria within canary window -> promote to staged rollout. If both meet criteria, choose lowest-cost path unless quality delta favors one.
Jared: One more thing — add a small A/B routing policy to send 5% of live traffic to canary if safe. Ops needs approval.
Sam: 5% traffic OK under canary SLA, but we require automatic rollback threshold locked in.
Maya: Great. I'll update the roadmap doc and the OKR ticket with owners and launch criteria. Pinning this thread to roadmap channel after we finalize. :rocket:
Lee: Thanks — I'll drop the kernel perf numbers by tomorrow.
Noah: I'll stand up dashboards and invite CS.
Jared: Will post the prototype branches and short README once scoped.
Maya: Thanks all, decision thread open until EOD Friday. :thinking:
